abandonment_clause: If G-SUB fails - none of the EIGHT G-SUB CANDIDATE configurations, including all_translation, reaches 8/16 grasp resets - then no single command channel carries the failure and the preregistered Outcome D abandonment clause of apple_policy_v1.md section 7 fires AS WRITTEN. This control line stops on this corpus and this camera. No further loss, head or output-parameterisation variant is preregistered on it. The next task is a perception/data task. Cohort C remains unconsumed. The executing agent stops and reports and does not select the follow-up itself. SUBJECT TO precedence_rule_D1_over_G_SUB: if CLAUSE (a) HOLDS BY EITHER DISJUNCT, this clause does NOT fire, once, and exemption_spent is set to true.

B1_harness_soundness.on_failure: every number in this task is void

baselines.B2_zero_substitution_control: the 'none' configuration must reproduce outputs/task056-cohort-d/a2.json: same single grasp seed (45100), same 16 termination reasons, same executed-step counts. If the harness changes the pure-policy result the harness is a confound and the sweep is void. This is the control that makes G-SUB interpretable and the one most likely to be skipped.
baselines.B3_inert_probe_tripwire_RUN_FIRST: the 'full' configuration (all seven dimensions from the shadow expert) must reach >= 14/16 grasp resets. If it does not, the substitution channel is not reaching the robot and the sweep is void before it starts. apple_policy_v1_results.md section 13 instance 9: a control whose output is indistinguishable from a real pass CONCEALS the class it was built to catch, so this one must fail loudly when inert.
baselines.B4_shadow_expert_is_not_an_input: behavioural test that the shadow command is computed strictly after policy.act returns and is never an argument to it, plus the ast.walk form (its text-grep predecessor produced a false positive on a correct runner) asserting policy.py imports no label or truth module. G6's zero-privileged-reads rule applies to the CONTROLLER; in a substituted configuration the expert IS part of the commanded action, hence the labelling rule.
baselines.B5_standing_offline_anchor: A1 0.011059 < A0 0.013129 < A2 0.017935 < A3 0.023404. The primary is third of four, beaten by the arm that never sees an image. Carried, not re-measured.
baselines.B6_does_the_learned_part_do_work: NOT DEMONSTRATED, on any metric. This task does not attempt to establish it. Every probe is diagnostic and no result here may be reported as progress toward a learned result.

cohort_discipline.cohort_C: NOT TOUCHED BY THIS TASK AT ANY STAGE. No gate references it. This protocol preregisters no use of it. The handover's blocking stored-values debt attaches to a runner that opens C; this protocol builds no such runner, so that debt does not land here and must not be discharged speculatively.
cohort_discipline.no_selection_on_D: D is a mechanism instrument, not a scoreboard. No checkpoint is chosen, retrained or tuned against a D outcome.
cohort_discipline.substituted_numbers_are_never_learned_re: Every configuration with a non-empty substitution set puts a privileged controller partly in command. Every number it produces is labelled non-learned in the table itself, not only in a footnote.

committed_in_advance: A rescue under expert substitution injects privileged information at 50 Hz, which the policy does not get. It shows WHICH CHANNEL the failure flows through; it does NOT show that a learned version of that channel is attainable. No D3 number may be read as evidence that a fix will work.

corrections_to_the_TASK_056_record_estab.1_the_hedging_signature_is_ABSENT_OFFLIN: TWO HALVES, AND ONLY ONE IS MEASURED. OFFLINE, measured on the validation split: the hedging signature is ABSENT -- saturated-row error is LOWER than unsaturated, conditional means reach 88-98% of the boundary on both signs, and the predicted-to-TARGET standard-deviation ratio is 0.952-0.980. The statistics the original reading was taken from could not have shown this either way: cloning.action_error's unconditional median necessarily sits inside the non-saturated group at 44.503% val saturation, and output_std_per_dimension is predictions only, so 'compressed' had no referent. ONLINE: whether dz behaviour caused the closed-loop failure is UNMEASURED and stays unmeasured, because the signs of every closed-loop command are unrecoverable. The prediction in apple_policy_v1.md section 12 and declared risk R5 range over BOTH halves, so the words 'refuted', 'contradicted' and 'did not occur' are NOT USED UNQUALIFIED anywhere; every statement carries 'offline' or 'on the validation split'. Expert saturation: 44.886% TRAIN, 44.503% VAL, reported separately.
corrections_to_the_TASK_056_record_estab.2_the_sign_of_every_TASK_056_command_is_: scripts/evaluate_policy.py computed every stored command statistic from np.abs(...). Zero negative numbers exist anywhere in command_statistics across all 64 attempts. |dz| q50 = 0.0125 is equally consistent with descending slowly, ascending slowly and oscillating about zero; |grasp| q50 = 1.0 is equally consistent with a hand held fully OPEN - which is what the expert does through orient and descend - and one held fully closed. The under-shoot reading in apple_policy_v1_results.md section 16 and task056_handover.md section 5 is therefore UNMEASURED rather than refuted. This is why D1-grasp is the most informative probe here.
corrections_to_the_TASK_056_record_estab.3_both_learned_arms_grasped_and_lifted_t: A2 on seed 45100 and A3 on seed 45006 each reached the scorer's grasp stage, lifted the apple +0.1678 m and +0.1694 m against a 0.05 m gate, and were STILL HOLDING IT, undropped, when the 1000-step cap ended the attempt. Neither reached transport. The 1/16 counts ARE in apple_policy_v1_results.md sections 14 and 16; the lift height, the sustained contact and the undropped state are nowhere in the record; and task056_handover.md gives neither arm's grasp count at all, stating only the controls' 0/16. The compression into the handover removed the run's single most encouraging measurement.
corrections_to_the_TASK_056_record_estab.4_the_near_constant_reading_is_translati: Median across attempts: dx q90/q50 1.00-1.22 and dz 1.01-1.32, versus droll q50 0.179-0.243, q90 0.478-0.498, q99 0.503-0.513 (ratio 2.05-2.67). Stated at that strength and no further: droll's out-of-distribution rate is 5-7% and its q90 sits at the 0.5 configured bound, which is LESS saturation than the expert's measured ~27% at |max|, so this is not roll running away. The observation is that the one dimension with real online variance is rotational, and it is the dimension with the SMALLEST offline error in Table A. Largest online/offline behavioural gap in the run, and not in the dimension the dz hypothesis pointed at.
corrections_to_the_TASK_056_record_estab.5_scope_correction_on_the_control_arms: A0 and A1: reach 0/16 each (latched; near = ||palm-apple|| <= 6.5 cm or hand_contact), hand_contact false at every attempt's end, final object_plate_distance_m within 0.1 mm of the report's own stored reset geometry on 16/16, and object_height_m a single value 0.766633 across all 32 attempts. Contact is the only route by which the robot can move the apple, so reach 0/32 establishes this independently of the distance statistic. A3 is NOT covered: its reach is 4/16 with five distinct heights. An earlier draft extended the statement to A3 from a mis-scoped count.
corrections_to_the_TASK_056_record_estab.6_no_statement_that_every_attempt_hit_th: A3 had two guard_refusal terminations, on seeds 45001 (157 executed steps) and 45003 (143). They are physical stops, not cap hits.

definitions_every_scope_term_used_in_a_g.arm_note: A4 is NOT an arm in this protocol. It is not built and this protocol does not propose building it.

configuration.defect_this_enumeration_fixes: An earlier draft defined a configuration as 'the named subset of the seven free dimensions' and let G-SUB range over ANY configuration. Under that wording 'full' IS a configuration, B3 requires full to reach >=14/16, and G-SUB passed if any configuration reached >=8/16 -- so B3 PASSING IMPLIED G-SUB PASSING while B3 FAILING VOIDED THE RUN, and the gate wired to the abandonment clause had NO FAILING PATH. The candidate list also existed only in the protocol's prose, never in the definitions and never in the gate: an unenumerated scope term deciding an outcome, verbatim the TASK-056 defect this section exists to prevent.

definitions_every_scope_term_used_in_a_g.departure_at_step_t: median over the six arm dimensions of |policy - shadow expert|
definitions_every_scope_term_used_in_a_g.grasp_reset: a development seed on which the latched score['grasp'] is true at any point

shadow_expert_command.consequence_for_D3_declared_before_any_n: A D3 configuration can inject a lift-phase ascent into an attempt whose hand has never closed on anything. A confound on the only gate. shadow_expert_phase is logged per step, and a G-SUB pass whose attempts spent most of their commands past the expert's close phase is REPORTED AS SUCH next to the pass. Reporting requirement, not a threshold.
shadow_expert_command.definition: OracleManipulationPolicy(sim.task_truth()).action(robot) at indices (6,7,8,9,10,11,13), advanced by advance(result) on every executed step, computed strictly AFTER policy.act returns
shadow_expert_command.it_is_a_HYBRID_reference_after_roughly_s: advance(result) is called on THE POLICY'S executed result, so the expert's phase counter advances on the policy's clock rather than its own progress. A policy that has gone nowhere still drives the reference into descend and then lift. It is 'expert targets on a policy-driven clock' and is named that way wherever used.
shadow_expert_command.it_is_exhausted_after_805_commands: scripted.py's phase table sums to 130+80+45+150+160+100+60+80 = 805 and action() RAISES once done. Every TASK-056 attempt not stopped by the embodiment ran to 1000, so the shadow expert dies around step 805 on nearly every attempt, and run_attempt's bare `except BaseException` would turn that into a dead run with no report.

definitions_every_scope_term_used_in_a_g.step_zero_command: the policy's 7-vector at the first act() call after robot.reset, before any execute()
definitions_every_scope_term_used_in_a_g.why: apple_policy_v1_results.md section 15: one undefined term ('learned arm', used thirteen times across the frozen artifacts, defined in none) decided whether an irreplaceable cohort would be consumed. Every scope term below is enumerated by name.

ClonedPolicy.implementation_sha256 is sha256(policy.py) and load() refuses a mismatch - demonstrated, not theoretical (apple_policy_v1_results.md section 9: a source fix made all four checkpoints unloadable).

runner_changes_landed_with_this_preregis.per_dimension_clip_counts: clipped_commands_per_dimension, alongside the any-dimension clipped_commands counter which keeps its former meaning exactly.
runner_changes_landed_with_this_preregis.signed_per_dimension_logging: command_statistics now records a 'signed' block per dimension ALONGSIDE the absolute fields, which keep their exact former values so reports stay comparable with TASK-056's. run_attempt also records first_command, the signed step-zero 7-vector.
runner_changes_landed_with_this_preregis.stage_label_defect_WITHDRAWN: A third requirement was proposed - that stages[t] is one step stale - and it is WRONG. scorer.evaluate() is the last statement of the loop body and robot.observe() the first of the next iteration, with nothing mutating the simulator between them, so the stage label is contemporaneous with the observation the command was computed from. Verified by tracing the ordering, not by reading. The claim is withdrawn rather than quietly dropped.

frozen_D1_thresholds_three_times_table_A: Derived from the ROUNDED Table A cells, which are the authority. Tripling an unrounded intermediate instead put the manifest 1e-6 out of agreement with its own table; a consistency test caught it before merge. HEADROOM CHECKED BEFORE THE RUN: Table A is an all-phase median while D1 is scored on reset (orient-phase) frames, so the populations differ. The worst realized orient-to-unconditional error ratio across all four arms and all seven dimensions is 1.313 (A2 right_dpitch), so the 3x threshold retains 2.28x headroom and a sound pipeline should pass D1 rather than fail it spuriously -- the property that had to hold for the precedence rule not to become an automatic exemption.

frozen_offline_conditionals_and_phase_ta.generating_script: scripts/measure_policy_offline_conditionals.py (committed). Reproduces every value in this block exactly. cloning.evaluate_policy CANNOT produce them: it returns one unconditional per-dimension median and the PREDICTIONS' std. A separate script rather than an edit to cloning.py, which participates in no checkpoint implementation_sha256 (VisualModel's digest covers models/base.py, the backend module, models/readout.py and readout_labels.py; ClonedPolicy's covers policy.py alone) but whose provenance surface stays untouched while any TASK-056 checkpoint must remain loadable.
frozen_offline_conditionals_and_phase_ta.reading_rule_for_the_phase_table_fixed_i: An OFFLINE error on recorded frames. A phase with a low error here is NOT thereby a phase the controller handles -- that is the covariate-shift gap this protocol exists to measure.

val_saturation.note: VAL rates. The committed 44.886% is the TRAIN cohort (68,791 rows).

frozen_offline_conditionals_and_phase_ta.why: cloning.action_error computes ONE unconditional per-dimension median over all rows; no saturated-row conditional exists in the file. Val saturation is 44.503%, below half, so that median necessarily sits inside the NON-saturated group and the cell is MATHEMATICALLY INCAPABLE of testing 'large error on the saturated rows'. output_std_per_dimension is PREDICTIONS ONLY -- target std is never computed, so 'compressed' had NO REFERENT. An earlier draft drew a conclusion from both; that conclusion is withdrawn and these conditionals replace it.

D1.derivation: the offline error is measured on recorded val frames at arbitrary phase; a reset frame is one specific in-distribution phase, so the claim tested is 'same order', not 'equal'. The per-dimension errors themselves span 4.50x, so a factor below 3 cannot be distinguished from ordinary per-dimension variation while 10x or more is unambiguous. A judgement call fixed before the numbers exist; realized ratios reported per dimension whatever they are.
D1.rule: passes for arm X iff, for EVERY one of the six arm dimensions, the median across the 16 seeds of |step-zero policy - shadow expert| is <= 3x X's own frozen_offline_error_table_A cell

D1_grasp.derived_two_sided_count: seeds where |step-zero right_grasp - (-1.0)| >= 1.0, equivalently where the commanded value is >= 0.0
D1_grasp.primary_report: the SIGNED step-zero right_grasp value, per arm per seed -- the full 4x16 table of numbers, not a count
D1_grasp.reading: the policy is not commanding the hand open at the one instant where the correct command is known and unambiguous
D1_grasp.reference: the expert's step-zero right_grasp is -1.0 EXACTLY on every reset (scripted.py orient phase), so no threshold is needed
D1_grasp.why_a_count_of_grasp_greater_than_zero_w: ONE-SIDED, and AN INERT POLICY PASSES IT: a head emitting exactly 0.0 scores ZERO sign errors and reads correct while being wrong by a full unit against a reference known exactly. That is the blind-baseline failure apple_policy_v1.md 5.1 was rewritten to remove, and the SECOND threshold in this design with that shape; the first was the original G-SUB.

D2.why_stated_this_way: apple_policy_v1.md section 5.3 announced a rule was 'not a gate' and then decided gate outcomes through the missing-values rule (apple_policy_v1_results.md section 15). D2 feeds nothing.

G_SUB.CORRECTION_carried_in_the_open: An earlier draft defended this gate against a demo_replay null of p0=1/3 and quoted 'the one-sided binomial probability of >= 8/16 is 0.189'. 0.189 IS WRONG: P(X>=8|n=16,p=1/3) = 0.126501. 0.189 corresponds to p0 = 0.363344, which nothing here uses. At the correct value the FAMILY-WISE probability across the eight candidates is 0.661077, so under that null the gate would have been near a coin flip rather than the screen it was presented as. The demo_replay null is DROPPED ENTIRELY: it is an open-loop baseline while G-SUB asks whether substitution moves THIS policy.
G_SUB.derivation_of_8_of_16: the midpoint between the pure-policy 1/16 = 6.25% and the 100% ceiling: the effect must be at least half the distance to the ceiling. A MAGNITUDE threshold, not a significance threshold; D is non-gating and no p-value from it is a result.
G_SUB.metric: grasp resets out of 16, per configuration, A2 only
G_SUB.null_defended_against: the PURE POLICY'S OWN RATE, 1/16 (outputs/task056-cohort-d/a2.json). That is the rate substitution must beat for substitution to have done anything, and the only null with a defensible claim to being this experiment's.
G_SUB.precision_note: Stored at full double precision rather than rounded. A consistency test recomputes each from the stated null and the enumerated candidate count; rounding made that test fail at 1e-6 and the fix is more digits, not a looser tolerance.

reference_points_fixed_before_the_run.scripted_oracle: 24/24 pooled on three prior wide cohorts

G_SUB.rule: passes iff at least one of the EIGHT G-SUB CANDIDATE configurations reaches >= 8/16 grasp resets. 'none' and 'full' are CONTROLS and NOT candidates, so a passing 'full' cannot pass the gate.

missing_values: A gate that cannot be evaluated counts as failed. D1 and G-SUB are the only gates.
not_done_declared: any model, loss, head or output-parameterisation change
the on-policy-relabeling argument for a follow-up, which is recorded in the results document as a named candidate and deliberately NOT preregistered here

pre_declared_outcomes.P: Clause (a) holds: D1 fails for >= 3 of the 4 arms, OR D1-grasp's two-sided count is >= 8/16 for >= 3 of the 4 arms. A locatable pipeline discrepancy. Next: an audit of the observation path from G1Embodiment.observe to ClonedPolicy.act against cloning.py's training path, then a re-measurement. No model change, no retrain.
pre_declared_outcomes.P_over_X_precedence: G-SUB fails AND clause (a) HOLDS BY EITHER DISJUNCT: OUTCOME P TAKES PRECEDENCE AND OUTCOME X DOES NOT FIRE, once. exemption_spent is set to true in the results document, and a re-run after the fix whose G-SUB fails with clause (a) not holding fires the abandonment clause as written.
pre_declared_outcomes.S: Clause (a) does NOT hold (D1 passes for >= 2 of the 4 arms AND D1-grasp's count is < 8/16 for >= 2 of the 4 arms) and G-SUB passes. The failing channel is named. Next: a new preregistration for a targeted fix, with its own controls. That task may ask for cohort C.
pre_declared_outcomes.V: B1, B2 or B3 fails. The run is void. No arm numbers are reported as results; the defect and the void are recorded.
pre_declared_outcomes.X: G-SUB fails AND clause (a) does NOT hold. The abandonment clause fires. The line stops.
pre_declared_outcomes.a_grasp_latched_before_exhaustion_still_: Under the definition of grasp_reset ('a development seed on which the latched score.grasp is true at any point'), termination by shadow_expert_exhausted ends the attempt but does not un-latch a stage already reached.

precedence_rule_D1_over_G_SUB.exemption_spent_contract: Frozen at false. The results document sets it true the first time the exemption is claimed. ANY SUCCESSOR PROTOCOL MUST CITE THIS FIELD IN ITS OWN GATE SECTION and may not claim the exemption while it reads true. Without a field to flip, 'once' is prose binding a document this protocol cannot reach.
precedence_rule_D1_over_G_SUB.keyed_on_clause_a_not_on_D1_alone: An earlier revision stated the precedence over the D1 disjunct only, so on (D1 passes all four, D1-grasp >= 8/16 for >= 3 arms, G-SUB fails) the success clause and Outcome P said continue while the abandonment clause and Outcome X said stop -- VERBATIM the contradiction the rule was written to remove, one disjunct over. The case is live rather than theoretical: grasp is a separate normalization path and the one dimension with an exactly-known reference, so it is the disjunct most likely to fire alone.
precedence_rule_D1_over_G_SUB.rule: CLAUSE (a) AS A WHOLE takes precedence -- EITHER DISJUNCT. If either D1 fails for >= 3 of the 4 arms OR D1-grasp's two-sided count is >= 8/16 for >= 3 of the 4 arms, the observation the controller receives is not the one the trainer used. G-SUB's result is then UNINTERPRETABLE RATHER THAN NEGATIVE -- a sweep conducted through a broken channel measures the channel. In that case the abandonment clause does NOT fire; the task reports a pipeline defect, and the line continues for the purpose of fixing it. THIS EXEMPTION IS AVAILABLE EXACTLY ONCE, tracked by exemption_spent; the D1_grasp disjunct is covered because the precedence is keyed on clause (a), not on D1 alone.
precedence_rule_D1_over_G_SUB.the_defect_it_fixes: An earlier revision had the abandonment clause fire unconditionally on a G-SUB failure while the success clause said the line continues if D1 fails for >=3 arms. On the joint outcome 'D1 fails for >=3 arms AND G-SUB fails' -- plausible, arguably the modal one -- one clause said stop and the other said continue, and the pre-declared outcomes listed both side by side with NO PRECEDENCE. A preregistration whose function is to bind the executing agent left the agent free to pick AFTER SEEING THE NUMBERS.
precedence_rule_D1_over_G_SUB.the_exemption_is_available_exactly_once: Once the defect is fixed, a re-run whose G-SUB fails with clause (a) not holding fires the clause as written. The exemption is recorded as spent by setting exemption_spent to true in the results document the first time it is claimed, so a second claim is visibly unavailable.
precedence_rule_D1_over_G_SUB.why_the_once_is_load_bearing: Without it this is an unbounded escape from abandonment, which is worse than the contradiction it replaces.

shadow_expert_exhaustion_preregistered_b.BLOCKING_DEFECT_THIS_FIXES: An earlier revision keyed the rule on 'D3', and 'none' IS a D3 configuration, so every 'none' attempt would have terminated at ~805 with shadow_expert_exhausted. B2 requires 'none' to reproduce outputs/task056-cohort-d/a2.json, whose sixteen attempts are ALL step_limit at exactly 1000 executed steps. B2 could never have passed, Outcome V would have fired, and THE RUN WOULD HAVE BEEN VOID WITH NO ARM NUMBERS REPORTED. 'full' was never at risk: orient+descend+close = 255 commands, +lift = 405, well inside 805. The second-order hazard is worse: a preregistration that provokes its own violation invites the executing agent to reason its way out of an obviously-unintended void mid-run, which is exactly what the process section's 'stops and reports rather than repairing as a reflex' exists to prevent.
shadow_expert_exhaustion_preregistered_b.empty_substitution_set: all of D1 and D2, AND the 'none' configuration of D3. The shadow expert is a RECORDING, not a command source, so its exhaustion cannot affect the robot. It stops being recorded, THE ATTEMPT CONTINUES TO ITS CAP, and the report records shadow_expert_exhausted_at_step. Departure past that step is null, NEVER zero.
shadow_expert_exhaustion_preregistered_b.non_empty_substitution_set: 'full' and the eight G-SUB candidates. The expert IS part of the commanded action, so at exhaustion the attempt TERMINATES with reason shadow_expert_exhausted and counts as a NON-SUCCESS. Not a concession: the oracle's budget is 805 commands and scripted_oracle succeeds inside it (24/24 pooled).
shadow_expert_exhaustion_preregistered_b.reported_for_every_attempt: shadow_expert_exhausted_at_step, so a reader can see how many attempts the rule bound.

success_clause: GOVERNED BY precedence_rule_D1_over_G_SUB, which ranges over CLAUSE (a) AS A WHOLE. Continues iff EITHER (a) D1 fails for >= 3 of the 4 arms, OR D1-grasp's TWO-SIDED count (seeds where |step-zero right_grasp - (-1.0)| >= 1.0) is >= 8/16 for >= 3 of the 4 arms - follow-up is a pipeline audit and re-measurement, NOT a model change and NOT a retrain; OR (b) G-SUB passes, naming the failing channel. If EITHER DISJUNCT of (a) holds AND G-SUB fails, clause (a) applies and the abandonment clause does not fire, ONCE. In both cases the follow-up is a NEW preregistration with its own gates and controls.
what_this_task_is: A DIAGNOSTIC task. It trains nothing, changes no model, and proposes no output-parameterisation change. Its only purpose is to locate the gap between TASK-056's near-perfect open-loop imitation and its closed-loop failure. Its single gate can fire the abandonment clause that apple_policy_v1.md section 7 already preregistered.
